title: Parisi's solution of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model from synchronous Monte Carlo dynamics
abstract: Sompolinsky and Zippelius obtained Parisi's solution of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model from the relaxational dynamics of soft spins in continuous time, by assuming a hierarchy of widely separated time scales. Here we carry out the same programme for a discrete-time dynamics in which all Ising spins are updated at once. This dynamics, synchronous Monte Carlo (SyncMC), introduces Gaussian auxiliary fields so that the spins become conditionally independent, and it samples the Boltzmann distribution exactly for any system with symmetric pairwise couplings. We show that, for any such system, the correlation and response functions of SyncMC obey an exact fluctuation-dissipation relation in discrete time in equilibrium. The dynamical mean-field equations of SyncMC for the SK model contain two terms absent in continuous-time dynamics, a self-coupling of each spin and a noise correlated through the couplings; both affect only the fast relaxation. As a result, under the same assumptions as in the Sompolinsky-Zippelius construction (widely separated time scales, and on each slow scale the same relation with a reduced ratio x, as expected in relaxation from random initial conditions), the long-time structure of SyncMC reproduces the Parisi equations, including the Parisi partial differential equation and the equation for the distribution of local fields. Equilibrium simulations with replica exchange for up to N=2048 spins exclude the replica-symmetric distribution of the actual local fields and are consistent with the Parisi solution. The function x(q) estimated from the overlap distribution, and from the response in relaxation from random configurations for up to N=4096 spins, is also consistent with Parisi's.
summary: This paper investigates the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model by analyzing its dynamics using synchronous Monte Carlo (SyncMC) updates. The authors show that the dynamics obey an exact fluctuation-dissipation relation and, under appropriate time-scale assumptions, the long-time behavior reproduces the established Parisi equations. This provides strong numerical and theoretical evidence supporting the Parisi solution over simpler mean-field approximations.
main_problem: To determine if the Parisi solution for the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick (SK) model, originally derived from continuous-time dynamics, can be reproduced using a discrete-time, synchronous Monte Carlo (SyncMC) dynamics.
main_result: The long-time structure of the SyncMC dynamics reproduces the Parisi equations, including the Parisi partial differential equation, and equilibrium simulations confirm consistency with the Parisi solution over replica-symmetric predictions.
method: The authors analyze the SyncMC dynamics by deriving its fluctuation-dissipation relation and applying a dynamical mean-field approach, assuming widely separated time scales.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model, a mean-field spin glass model characterized by random, symmetric pairwise couplings. The dynamics are simulated using a synchronous Monte Carlo (SyncMC) update rule.
key_observables: Correlation function, response function, overlap distribution $x(q)$, and the fluctuation-dissipation ratio $x(q)$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), system size ($N$), and the assumption of widely separated time scales ($	au_K \ll \dots \ll 	au_0$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the assumption of widely separated time scales and that the SyncMC dynamics possesses an exact discrete-time fluctuation–dissipation relation.
figures_summary: Figures compare the self-overlap $q_{cl}(	au)$ and the fluctuation-dissipation ratio $x(q)$ for various system sizes ($N$) against the theoretical predictions, showing agreement with the Parisi structure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the exact fluctuation-dissipation relation for SyncMC. It then applies a dynamical mean-field theory approach, assuming multi-time-scale separation, to derive the effective process equations. Finally, it compares the long-time behavior of these equations and numerical simulations against the known Parisi equations.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous dynamical confirmation of the Parisi solution using a different, discrete-time simulation scheme (SyncMC), which is valuable for understanding the robustness of mean-field results in complex dynamics.
